Do You Have”Eldest Daughter Syndrome?” Gabriel Applauds $6M in Security Grants for the Valley See Page 11 Volume 5, Issue 94 Top California Laws Impacting Business in 2024 See Page 5 See Page 6 ENCINO ENTERPRISE NEWS IN BRIEF Friends of the LA River Earth Day Event April 20 Friends of the LA River, alongside volunteers at the Encino Neighborhood Council, will gather for their Earth Day event on Saturday, April 20, from 8 am to 12 pm at the Sepulveda Basin Wildlife Reserve (6350 Woodley Ave). Join them for a morning of habitat restoration removing invasive plant species, create and take home handmade seedballs and partake on a nature walk along the reserve with the San Fernando Valley Audubon Society. RSVP to this free event at support.folar.org/event/earth-day-habitat-restore-and-renew/ e565781. Hope of the Valley Expanding to Encino? Hope of the Valley, now known as Hope the Mission, has proposed an expansion into Encino with conversion of the Rodeway Inn (also known as Oak Tree Inn) into housing for “at risk youth” who may be aging out of the foster care system. Currently the hotel at 17448 Ventura Blvd. at Encino Avenue is a 9,286-square-foot building with a two-story center and two one-story wings with 65 rooms. The hotel was built in 1949 and recently remodeled in 2018. Founded in 2009, Hope of the Valley Rescue Mission began as a small ministry run out of Sun Valley where volunteers cooked and served hot meals to homeless men, women and children. A Compendious Source of Information April 19, 2024 Day of Service Creates “World’s Largest Lasagna” to Feed Angelenos in Need Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel was joined by over 1,300 volunteers, 50 community groups, and other elected officials on April 14 to participate in nearly 20 service projects across the San Fernando Valley as part of the Assemblymember’s Third Annual Valley Day of Service. “While social media is often filled with negativity, the truth is we are lucky to have such a generous and caring community in the San Fernando Valley,” said Assemblymember Gabriel. “I am grateful for all of the amazing volunteers who turned out despite the rain to make this Day of Service such a success, and I am thankful for the wonderful community organizations that help make a positive difference in the Valley every day of the year.” Projects at the Valley Day of Service included: -Assembling of “The World’s Largest Lasagna” by preparing 22,000 meals for Angelenos in need with Hope the Mission. -Packing 2,000 homeless outreach kits with LA Family Housing and Jewish Family Service LA. Tarzana Music Night April 26 Join Tarzana Community and Cultural Center for another “Music Night Live” on Friday, April 26, from 7 to 10 pm. Performers include Tracy Newman, Art Podell, Brent Hahn, Kevin Kelso, Kathleen Kelso, Kim Margolis, Claire Bloom, Dr. Generous, Dave Morrison, Karen Turner, James Combs & Erin Hawkins, Justin Richard, Steven Wagner and Annette Adler. Special guest JaKL will perform a 20-minute set at 8 pm. The show will be outdoors and refreshments will be available for purchase. Tickets are $5 at the door or through mytarzana.org. Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel, center, his son Joshua (6), and volunteers help prepare “The World’s Largest Lasagna” — 22,000 servings of lasagna for Angelenos in need. -Making 1,000 sandwiches for those experiencing hunger with Project Rise for West Valley Food Pantry, About My Father’s Business, First United Methodist Church Kingdom Food Pantry, and Hope the Mission -Writing over 1,000 letters to seniors at ONEgeneration, health care workers at Valley Presbyterian Hospital, and cancer patients at City of Hope. -Crafting 1,000 paracord bracelets for active duty service members with Operation Gratitude and assembling more than 600 tote bags for seniors at ONEgeneration. -Cleaning up the Sepulveda Basin with Volunteers Cleaning Communities. -Planting fruit trees with Tree People and the San Fernando Valley Rose Society at the Hope the Mission family shelter. -Beautifying and renovating the New Economics for Women campus in Canoga Park. -Preparing a community mural with Arts Bridging the Gap at the West Valley YMCA in Reseda. -Training more than 100 volunteers in CPR with the American Red Cross. -Hosting a blood drive with Cedars-Sinai to donate 36 pints of blood. -Planting a new native plant garden with the Santa Monica Mountains Fund and San Fernando Valley Audubon Society at the Mid Valley YMCA. - Crafting 35 blankets for survivors of domestic violence at Haven Hills. -Helping to find a new home for eight dogs adopted from Foxy and the Hounds.
Gabriel Applauds $6 Million in Security Grants for the Valley Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel recently announced that the State of California has awarded $40 million in security grants to nonprofits facing hate motivated violence — including over $6 million awarded to nonprofits serving residents of Assembly District 46 in the San Fernando Valley. In total, 29 nonprofits that serve Assembly District 46 residents were awarded $6.1 million for critical security enhancements to their facilities. Nearly $3 million in funding was allocated to nonprofits located within Assembly District 46, including the Holy Martyrs Armenian Apostolic Church in Encino, the AGBU Manoogian- Demirdjian School in Canoga Park, Valley Beth Shalom in Encino, Valley Presbyterian Hospital in Van Nuys, Crespi Carmelite High School in Encino, De Toledo High School in West Hills, and Chabad of the Valley in Tarzana. “I’m grateful that the State of California is providing critical security funding to so many worthy nonprofits across the San Fernando Valley,” said Gabriel, who serves as Co-Chair of the Legislative Jewish Caucus and who authored the legislation to create the NSGP. “California will not stand idly by as hate and antisemitism continue to rise and while our vulnerable communities are threatened by extremists. This security funding will support critical security enhancements at institutions most in need and will make it clear that California stands with all communities targeted by hate.” The NSGP has provided critical security funding to nonprofits at risk of hate- motivated violence – including $140 million over the last three state budget cycles. This year’s awards total $40 million. In 2019, Assemblymember Gabriel authored AB 1548, which created the NSGP. He authored AB 1664 in 2022, which made the NSGP permanent, increased the maximum grant to $500,000, and allowed funding to be used for security training. Last year Gabriel authored AB 1185, which broadens the reach of the NSGP and helps to ensure that funding is directed to applicants who are most likely to be targeted by hate- motivated violence. The NSGP has become the most popular grant administered by the Governor’s Office of Emergency Services and has been a critical lifeline for diverse faith communities, LGBTQ community centers, reproductive health facilities, and other nonprofits facing hate- motivated violence. On February 20, the LA City Council adopted a motion (Council File No. 23-1339) that mandates the development of a new Van Nuys Airport (VNY) Specific Plan. This plan will consider existing environmental, aeronautical, economical and home environment interests of the City, specifically the Valley. The motion also mandates the formation of the VNY Specific Plan Citizens Advisory Committee which will include at least one representative from CD 2, CD 3, CD 4, CD 5, CD 6 and CD 12. Council District 6 will be responsible for the formation and operation of this committee. Residents should contact their respective Neighborhood Council to submit their interest in participating on the committee. For organizational and vetting purposes, only candidates submitted by each qualifying Neighborhood Council President will be considered. For those interested, one mandated qualifying criteria for candidates listed is their ability to demonstrate that they reside in the district their respective Neighborhood Council represents. The deadline for submissions is May 6, 2024. City Council Calls for a Van Nuys Airport Citizens Advisory Committee Encino Enterprise, April 19, 2024, Page 11 REAL ESTATE
